observations.observation: The July 20, 2016 base panel already displays a large white area over labeled Osborn, leaving imagery visible along the west and south. This is a raster publication; it cannot prove the identity of a PDF mask object.

The May 31, 2024 annotated enclosure displays a similar large white area. PR #17 established that an opaque PDF MASK layer covers existing hazard graphics. This comparison is visual, not an exact registered boundary comparison.

A legacy blanking treatment retained during revision is a plausible explanation. The 2016 FIS recorded no identified SFHA for Osborn, whereas the 2024 determination adds Zone A and shaded Zone X. These observations support investigating a retained cartographic mask, but do not prove an accidental omission, FEMA intent, or which hidden graphics are operative.
observations.source: base panel + prior mask audit + historical FIS context

observations.observation: The determination revises Osborn's effective NFIP map and directs use of the annotated enclosures for floodplain management and insurance. It identifies changes from unshaded Zone X to Zone A and shaded Zone X, retains stricter state/local requirements, and says the base FIRM will not be physically republished at that time. It does not explain the mask.

The June 14, 2024 Federal Register notice states the listed flood hazard determinations are finalized after the notice/appeal process. The Osborn row identifies case 22-01-0871P, CID 230595 and May 31, 2024. This independently corroborates finalization; it does not identify individual polygon vertices or resolve the masked display.
